specification.problem: Min-plus witness search: for fixed source u and target v on a tiny weighted graph with n<=8 vertices, find d'(u,v)=min_w (D[u,w]+W[w,v]) by Grover-based minimum finding (Durr-Hoyer) over the intermediate vertex index w. This is the generic primitive named in the sketch, not the paper's subcubic hybrid algorithms.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One (u,v) pair, n<=8 (index register <=3 qubits), small integer weights. The runner builds a threshold-marking Grover oracle and one or more Grover rounds, with classical threshold updating. Outside scope: the subcubic O(n^{2.5-eps}) algorithms for small integer weights, geometric weights, few weights per vertex, and earliest arrivals; the classical matrix-multiplication/sampling balancing; QRAM cost accounting; all-pairs union bound. The abstract does not give these constructions.

symbols.meaning: candidate cost D[u,w]+W[w,v] for the fixed pair (u,v)
current threshold (best cost found so far)
2^q, size of index space, q=ceil(log2 n)

equations.label: Min-plus witness definition
equations.description: Target quantity per pair, found as minimum over witnesses.
equations.abstract_quote: The trivial classical algorithm for APSP and most all pairs path problems runs in $O(n^{3})$ time
equations.justification: The n^3 trivial algorithm and n^2.5 Grover search over n witnesses per pair imply this min-plus form; the exact formula is from the sketch and standard background.
assumptions: Fixed pair (u,v); D and W given as classical tables

equations.label: Threshold marking oracle
equations.description: Phase oracle marking witnesses strictly better than the threshold; the value and compare ancillas are uncomputed to |0>. For tiny instances, the runner may implement it as multi-controlled Z on index bit patterns in S_tau, computed classically from the table (the table is known to the builder in simulation).
equations.justification: Proposed construction following the sketch's compare-and-flip oracle; the abstract gives no circuit.
assumptions: Costs c(w) available to the oracle via lookup (QRAM assumption)
In the simulation, S_tau is encoded by the builder; a real hidden black box would be a placeholder

equations.label: Grover iterate and success probability
equations.description: After k iterations on the uniform superposition, measuring the index gives a marked witness with probability P_k. Optimal k is about floor(pi/(4 theta)).
equations.justification: Standard Grover analysis; the abstract only mentions Grover search.
assumptions: Indices w>=n are never marked, and N=2^q may exceed n

equations.label: Threshold update rule
equations.description: Durr-Hoyer loop: measure w_t after k_t random-bounded Grover iterations, verify classically, and lower the threshold. Stop when no improvement for a fixed number of rounds, or about 22.5 sqrt(n)+1.4 log^2 n total iterations in the original analysis.
equations.justification: Durr-Hoyer minimum finding, named in the sketch; constants are recalled, not from the abstract.
assumptions: Random k_t drawn uniformly from {0..ceil(sqrt(N))-1} or growing schedule

equations.label: Query complexity target
equations.latex: T_{\text{pair}}=\tilde O(\sqrt n),\quad T_{\text{APSP,trivial}}=n^2\tilde O(\sqrt n)=\tilde O(n^{2.5})
equations.description: The trivial quantum bound the paper improves to O(n^{2.5-eps}) for structured inputs.
equations.abstract_quote: the trivial algorithm in the quantum setting runs in $\tilde{O}(n^{2.5})$ time, using Grover search
equations.justification: The abstract states the trivial bound; the per-pair sqrt(n) split is the natural reading.

registers.name: idx
registers.role: witness index w, little-endian: qubit i is bit i of w

registers.name: val
registers.size: O(log(nW)), omitted in tiny instances if the oracle is compiled from the table
registers.role: candidate cost register for the adder-based oracle

registers.name: creg
registers.role: classical bits measuring idx; counts key last char is bit 0

specification.initial_state: |0>^{q} on idx (ancillas |0>), then H on every idx qubit to give the uniform superposition over w.

steps.description: Classically choose the initial threshold tau_0=c(w_0) for random w_0 (or w_0=0).
Build the circuit: H on idx, then k repetitions of oracle O_tau followed by diffusion (H, X, multi-controlled Z, X, H) on idx; measure idx into creg.
Read the measured w (reverse the counts string for bit order), classically verify c(w)<tau, and update tau.
Repeat with fresh random k until m=0 is reached or the iteration budget is exhausted. The final tau is d'(u,v).

specification.measurement: Measure only the idx qubits, one round per circuit; bit i of w corresponds to classical bit i.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Verify each measured witness against the table, track the minimum, and output the final threshold and its witness; stop after a fixed number of non-improving rounds.
assumptions: Scope choice: a single pair (u,v), n<=8, instead of full APSP.
The oracle is compiled from the classical table, since the true QRAM and black box are unavailable.
If the runner supplies a hidden black box, the oracle must be a placeholder call, and only the threshold comparison is built around it.
Ties are broken by strict inequality c(w)<tau.
missing_information: Actual subcubic constructions: small-integer-weight hybrid with threshold parameter, geometric weights, few-weights-per-vertex, earliest arrivals
Cost balance and the value of eps
Exact oracle interface and query budget of the runner
